source_book: Sri Chaitanya — IPE STUDY MATERIAL for Jr. Students, Physics (2026-27 edition)
note: Question index for diffing and authoring: VSAQ 20, SAQ 9, LAQ 0 (the chapter prints no LONG ANSWER section), PROBLEM 8 numbered questions (10 entries after splitting the printed parts of problems 1 and 8). The FORMULAE block on scan p.9 (printed p.11, left column) is not indexed. Stems restated in our own wording; the physics is exact. No solution content from the source book appears in this file, by policy. Single asterisks mark five questions; no question carries more than one.

questions.stem: Define instantaneous velocity. How is it found from a graph?
State the differences between distance and displacement.
What is the difference between average speed and instantaneous speed?
A car moves with uniform acceleration. Write the relation connecting its displacement, initial velocity, acceleration and time.
What is rectilinear motion? Give one example.
Define average acceleration. What is its SI unit?
What is free fall? State the value and the direction of the acceleration in free fall.
The instantaneous speed is always equal to the magnitude of the instantaneous velocity. Why?
Explain how the area under a velocity-time graph gives the displacement.
Can a body have zero velocity and non-zero acceleration at the same instant? Explain.
A car accelerates uniformly from 10 m/s to 20 m/s in 5 seconds. Calculate the acceleration.
An object is thrown vertically upwards with a velocity of 30 m/s. What is its velocity after 2 seconds? Take g = 9.8 m/s².
A car moving at 72 km/h is brought to rest in 10 seconds. Find the distance it covers before it stops.
The velocity of a particle is given by v(t) = 3t². Find its acceleration at t = 2 s.
A train starts from rest and reaches a velocity of 36 km/h in 10 s. Assuming uniform acceleration, calculate the acceleration and the distance covered in this time.
A ball is dropped from a height of 20 m. Find the time it takes to reach the ground. Take g = 10 m/s².
questions.notes: Printed typo: the bracket reads "(Takeg g = 10m/s²)"; read as "Take g = 10 m/s²".

questions.stem: A man walks 2 km in 30 minutes and returns by the same path in 20 minutes. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
An object moves with uniform acceleration and covers 100 m in 5 seconds. Its initial velocity is 4 m/s. Find the acceleration.

A police van moving on a highway at 30 km h⁻¹ fires a bullet at a thief's car that is moving away in the same direction at 192 km h⁻¹. The muzzle speed of the bullet is 150 m s⁻¹. With what speed does the bullet hit the thief's car?
A ruler falls freely and travels 20 cm before it is caught. Estimate the reaction time of the person. Use g = 10 m/s².
Derive the equation v = u + at using calculus.
Derive the equation s = ut + (1/2)at² using the graphical method.
Derive the kinematic equation of motion v² = v₀² + 2ax.
A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a velocity of 20 m/s from a height of 25 m. Calculate the time taken to reach the ground.
questions.notes: Ambiguous datum: the question does not state a value of g; the book's working takes g = 9.8 m/s².

questions.stem: Explain Galileo's law of odd numbers with a suitable example.
A man walks 2.5 km to a market at a speed of 5 km/h and returns at 7.5 km/h. Find his average speed and his average velocity.
questions.notes: Same data as prob1 (the NCERT home-to-market problem); this SAQ version asks for the round trip only, with no time interval.

questions.stem: Draw a position-time graph for a body moving with uniform acceleration. Explain how velocity is found from it.
Explain with an example why the instantaneous acceleration can be non-zero even when the instantaneous velocity is zero.
Define reaction time. Describe an experiment to measure it using a ruler.

A man walks on a straight road from his home to a market 2.5 km away at a speed of 5 km h⁻¹. He finds the market closed, turns back at once and walks home at a speed of 7.5 km h⁻¹. Find the magnitude of his average velocity over the time interval 0 to 50 min.
questions.notes: Printed as one question with parts (a) and (b) sharing the same stem; the printed text does not end with a question mark. Same data as saq6.

questions.stem: A man walks on a straight road from his home to a market 2.5 km away at a speed of 5 km h⁻¹. He finds the market closed, turns back at once and walks home at a speed of 7.5 km h⁻¹. Find his average speed over the time interval 0 to 50 min.
questions.notes: Part (b) of the printed question; see part (a).

questions.stem: A car travels the first third of a distance at a speed of 10 kmph, the second third at 20 kmph and the last third at 60 kmph. What is its mean speed over the whole distance?

A bullet moving at a speed of 150 m s⁻¹ strikes a tree and goes 3.5 cm into it before it stops. What is the magnitude of its retardation inside the tree, and how long does it take to stop after striking the tree?
A motorist drives north for 30 min at 85 km/h and then stops for 15 min. He then continues north and covers 130 km in 2 hours. What is his total displacement and his average velocity?

A ball A is dropped from the top of a building, and at the same instant an identical ball B is thrown vertically upward from the ground. When the balls collide, the speed of A is twice the speed of B. At what fraction of the height of the building does the collision happen?

Drops of water fall at regular time intervals from the roof of a building of height 16 m. The first drop strikes the ground at the same moment as the fifth drop leaves the roof. Find the distances between successive drops.

A hunter aims a gun at a monkey hanging from a tree some distance away. The monkey lets go of the branch at the moment the gun is fired, hoping to avoid the bullet. Explain why the monkey made a wrong move.
questions.notes: The book's working uses a line-of-sight figure (bullet fired at angle θ, monkey directly above the landing point); the question itself is fully stated in words.

questions.stem: A food packet is dropped from an aeroplane that is moving horizontally at 360 kmph, from a height of 500 m. Find its time of descent.
questions.notes: Printed as one question with parts (i) and (ii). Ambiguous datum: no value of g is stated; the book's working takes g = 10 m/s².

questions.stem: A food packet is dropped from an aeroplane that is moving horizontally at 360 kmph, from a height of 500 m. Find the horizontal distance between the point where the packet reaches the ground and the point on the ground directly below where it was dropped.
questions.notes: Part (ii) of the printed question; see part (i) for the g ambiguity.
